To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the more constrained group structures, in which members of a group have more limited access to the information of the other members, outperform the more open and free flowing structures.

the more constrained group structure outperforms the group structure with a free flow in both individual and collective accuracy, and this effect is due to the more constrained group's higher diversity.
the more constrained communication network, i.e. the small world network, outperforms the free communication network, i. e. the complete network, in terms of collective accuracy.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the structure of a group affects the performance of a group in a way that can be explained theoretically.
the question of what kind of group structure is best in terms of group accuracy.
the question of how to design groups in a way that improves group accuracy.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the kind of group you belong to does matter for group accuracy.
a small world structure outperforms a complete network in terms of both individual accuracy and collective accuracy.
the small world network is the best network structure to achieve group accuracy, because it is more effective than the complete network, and it is less costly than the complete network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the small world network structure is the most efficient structure for groups to reach high accuracy in the context of group decision making.
the kind of group you would want to belong to, is the kind that is structured in a way that maximizes the accuracy of the group's judgment.
the more constrained group structure (small world) is more accurate than the group with free flow of information (complete network).
The main takeaway from our work is that
group structure is an important factor to consider when studying the wisdom of crowds.
the kind of group structure you want to belong is one in which the group is not overly diverse, and in which the members of the group are not overly dependent on one another.
group structures may systematically affect group accuracy and that this effect is not a simple consequence of the amount of communication among group members.
